title: 106 Ridge Street
description: A 1914 Colonial Revival tenement on the corner of Ridge and Rivington Streets on the Lower East Side: six storeys of brick and fire escapes on a narrow Manhattan street grid, photographed from across the intersection.

attribution.title: File:Apartment building at 106 Ridge Street, Lower East Side, Manhattan - 20200906.jpg
attribution.creator: Andre Carrotflower

notes: Position and heading: Commons {{Location}} geotag with compass heading (accuracy unknown).

The published file is a 2586x2586 square crop of a 4:3 iPhone frame, so the EXIF focal length (29 mm eq.) does not give the FOV directly: full-frame hfov would be 61.6°, a centred crop without rescaling 41.9°; 48° assumes a 3024-px square crop. Calibrate.
Pitch 20° estimated by eye from pedestrians' head height (≈ 91% of the image height).
Resected from 3 ground + 3 vertical-edge correspondences picked on the photo (data/calibration/nyc-ridge-street.json); rms 33.3 px. Geotag was 0.0 m away. No building height was used.

Resection history: the maintainer resection above (position (-36.875, -33.871), heading 48.57°, pitch 17.07°, roll 1.34°, hfov 41.9°, all marked manual) was about 10° off in heading and 2° in roll. Its vertex-1 picks (data/calibration/nyc-ridge-street.json) mark the end of the ornate bays, not the end of the 28 m OSM edge, and are 433 px off under the camera below (docs/research/alignment.md §1).

Fixture camera auto-aligned from facade regularity (autoAlignCamera in web/src/lib/align.ts, with the resection relaxed from manual to inferred and hfov bounded to the EXIF range [41.9°, 61.6°]): heading 48.6° → 59.2°, roll 1.3° → -0.6°, moved 10.2 m along the Ridge Street facade and 0.7 m away from it; pitch 17.1° and hfov 41.9° (at the lower EXIF bound) kept. Window rows now level to 0.11 m instead of 0.80 m (robust σ) and all 92 windows land on the target or 202 Rivington instead of 88 with 4 missed. Values rounded; provenance inferred, so the app keeps refining it on load.
